title: Kubernetes on Oxide: How Customer Needs Shaped Our Integrations | Oxide Computer Company
excerpt: How customer needs shaped Oxide's Kubernetes integrations.
content_html:
In late 2024, customers and prospects were eager to run Kubernetes on Oxide, but we had no supported integrations to help them do it.

Kubernetes and Oxide are a natural fit. Kubernetes defines the infrastructure behavior it expects through standard extension points, while Oxide exposes the primitives needed to implement that behavior through APIs. The foundation for integration was there. What was missing was the software and an understanding of which integrations customers actually needed.

That was the situation when I joined Oxide as its first Solutions Software Engineer,[1] focused on building software to solve customer problems. My first assignment was to make it easier to deploy and operate Kubernetes on Oxide.

In my first week, I was handed two resources to help me get started:

  1. A customer-submitted pull request for a Rancher node driver

  2. An early draft of RFD 493 Initial Kubernetes Integrations

What began with those two resources grew into a team effort shaped by a feedback loop. Rather than design integrations in the abstract, we followed the problems customers encountered as they moved from provisioning clusters to operating workloads.

This post follows those problems across the Kubernetes lifecycle rather than in strict chronological order. Different provisioning workflows led us to Rancher, Omni, and Cluster API. Running clusters required infrastructure reconciliation, exposing applications revealed networking gaps, and stateful workloads exposed storage constraints. At each stage, customer workflows exposed the next gap, shaping both the integrations we built and the platform work still ahead.

How do I provision a Kubernetes cluster on Oxide?

The first gap we tackled was provisioning. Our immediate goal was to unblock the customer who had submitted the Rancher node driver pull request. Working through their use case would also give us firsthand experience creating Kubernetes clusters on Oxide and help us uncover the next problems to solve.

No single provisioning approach fit all customers' workflows, so we ended up publishing three integrations.

Rancher Node Driver

Before we could maintain the customer-submitted integration, we needed to understand the workflow it supported. I had never used Rancher or worked with a node driver, so reviewing the contribution meant learning both.

A Rancher node driver is an executable plugin that teaches Rancher how to create and manage virtual machines on a particular infrastructure platform. The Oxide Rancher node driver translates those operations into Oxide API requests. Once installed in Rancher, it lets customers provision Oxide instances as nodes in Rancher-managed Kubernetes clusters.

Testing confirmed that the customer’s implementation worked. I merged the pull request, added CI/CD and documentation improvements, and published the initial release. Oxide officially had its first Kubernetes integration—​and a customer was already using it successfully in production!

If you’re a Rancher shop looking to run Kubernetes on Oxide, see our Rancher guide to get started.

Omni Infrastructure Provider

Customers expressed interest in using Sidero Labs' Omni to provision Kubernetes clusters running Talos Linux. Omni connects to infrastructure platforms through infrastructure providers, programs that create Talos Linux instances and register them with Omni.

With KubeCon North America 2025 a few months away, we saw an opportunity to partner with Sidero Labs to build and showcase an Oxide infrastructure provider for Omni. We had seven weeks to complete it before our Oxide+Sidero event.[2] Building against a second provisioning platform would also test Oxide’s APIs across distinct customer workflows.

The integration work uncovered several issues across Omni and Talos Linux. I brought those issues to Sidero Labs in siderolabs/omni#1633, where their team was eager to work with us—​a lovely reminder of RFD 68 Partnership as Shared Values.

The most memorable issue was siderolabs/talos#11948. Oxide uses a FAT12 filesystem for cloud-init user-data, not ISO 9660, but Talos’s filesystem probe only attempted to read an ISO 9660 superblock from the NoCloud configuration disk. When that read failed, the probe stopped instead of trying other formats such as VFAT or MS-DOS. As a result, Talos never read the Oxide user-data containing the configuration needed to join Omni. The fix would not be released in time for KubeCon, leaving us with a rather funny workaround.

The workaround right now is to pad the user-data with comments to increase its size enough that it uses an ISO 9660 superblock.

KubeCon arrived and we hosted an Oxide+Sidero event to showcase the Oxide infrastructure provider for Omni. Customers could now use this infrastructure provider to provision Oxide instances running Talos Linux as nodes in Omni-managed Kubernetes clusters.

If you’re an Omni or Talos Linux shop looking to run Kubernetes on Oxide, see our Omni guide to get started.

Cluster API Provider

We knew we wanted to build an infrastructure provider for Kubernetes Cluster API (CAPI) when we first wrote RFD 493 Initial Kubernetes Integrations. Cluster API offered something our first two integrations did not—​an upstream, provider-extensible API for managing clusters without requiring a third-party platform like Rancher or Omni.

CAPI lets operators declaratively create, scale, upgrade, and delete Kubernetes clusters through Kubernetes custom resources. Infrastructure providers handle the platform-specific work, such as creating and deleting virtual machines. Building one is a significant investment. At the time, customer demand and engineering capacity did not yet justify that investment, so the project was deferred.

Eventually, both changed. Customers began asking for a CAPI provider, and the Solutions Software Engineering team grew. My teammates Josh and Brandon took ownership of the work and released Cluster API Provider Oxide (CAPOx), giving customers a Kubernetes-native way to provision clusters on Oxide.

The Cluster API workflow also exercises several of our other integrations, allowing us to dogfood[3] the end-to-end cluster workflow. The Kubernetes Image Builder uses our Packer plugin to create CAPI-ready Oxide VM images, which CAPOx uses when provisioning instances. Clusters provisioned with CAPOx also use the separately installed Oxide cloud controller manager (CCM) to integrate Kubernetes with Oxide at runtime.

If you want to provision Kubernetes clusters on Oxide with Cluster API, see our Cluster API guide to get started.

How does Kubernetes track Oxide instances?

Provisioning integrations create and manage Oxide instances, but they do not reconcile those instances with Kubernetes Node objects. Without that reconciliation, a cluster could not reliably determine whether an unreachable Kubernetes node was temporarily unavailable or whether its backing Oxide instance had been deleted.

We needed a component that ran in each cluster, spoke to the Oxide API, and continuously reconciled Oxide infrastructure with Kubernetes state. Kubernetes provides a standard extension point for this purpose: the cloud controller manager (CCM). A CCM lets infrastructure-specific controllers integrate Kubernetes resources with an infrastructure provider’s API without adding provider-specific code to Kubernetes itself.

We built the Oxide cloud controller manager to connect Kubernetes with Oxide. Its node controller keeps Kubernetes Node objects synchronized with their backing Oxide instances, recording details such as instance IDs and network addresses, and reporting whether each instance is running, shut down, or no longer exists. Kubernetes uses this information to initialize nodes and safely remove them when their backing instances are deleted.

The CCM does not create instances or provision clusters. That remains the job of provisioning integrations such as the Rancher node driver, the Omni infrastructure provider, and CAPOx. Instead, it provides a runtime integration shared across those provisioning workflows.

Importantly, building the CCM gave us a durable extension point inside each cluster. As Oxide evolves, we can add new infrastructure-aware controllers to the CCM rather than update every provisioning integration.

With that runtime extension point in place, we could address another layer of the Kubernetes experience: exposing applications. The CCM architecture also defines a service controller for Kubernetes LoadBalancer services, giving us a place to address the next customer problem.

How do I use LoadBalancer services?

One of the capabilities customers expect from cloud-integrated Kubernetes is support for Service objects of type LoadBalancer. When a user creates one, Kubernetes asks the cloud provider’s service controller to provision the necessary infrastructure and publish its address in the Service status. There was just one problem: Oxide did not yet offer a native load balancer.

Oxide did, however, have floating IPs. Floating IPs are addresses from a rack’s external IP pools that can be attached to and detached from instances, making those instances reachable from outside their VPCs. Using floating IPs offered a way to unblock LoadBalancer services. A floating IP would deliver traffic to a single Kubernetes node, and the Kubernetes Service dataplane could distribute that traffic to the appropriate pods.

Making that work required accounting for how Oxide floating IPs appear to an instance. They are transparent to the guest in two important ways. First, Oxide translates the destination address of inbound traffic to the instance’s internal IP before sending the traffic to the instance. Second, the instance has no network interface configured with the floating IP.

The resulting traffic flow looks like this:

Traffic flow to a LoadBalancer service using floating IPs.

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Client                                                     │
│ Request to floating IP: 45.154.216.233:80                  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Oxide networking                                           │
│ Translates destination to internal IP: 172.30.0.5:80       │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Kubernetes node                                            │
│ Packet arrives at internal IP: 172.30.0.5:80               │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Kubernetes Service dataplane                               │
│ Selects a Service endpoint                                 │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Pod                                                        │
│ Receives traffic on its target port                        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

That address translation created a subtle integration problem. The Kubernetes Service dataplane needed to treat the node’s internal IP as a Service frontend because that was the destination address packets actually carried when they reached the guest. The service controller therefore publishes two entries in status.loadBalancer.ingress:[4]

  1. The attached floating IP in Proxy mode

  2. The node’s internal IP in VIP mode

The status entries look like this:

status:
  loadBalancer:
    ingress:
      - ip: 45.154.216.233
        ipMode: Proxy
      - ip: 172.30.0.5
        ipMode: VIP

As a result, the kubectl output looks a little unusual:

$ kubectl get service nginx
NAME    TYPE           CLUSTER-IP       EXTERNAL-IP                 PORT(S)        AGE
nginx   LoadBalancer   10.106.122.233   45.154.216.233,172.30.0.5   80:30605/TCP   37h

Users see both the floating IP and the node’s internal IP in the EXTERNAL-IP column, even though only the floating IP is externally reachable. This is an imperfect abstraction, but it allows us to support a common Kubernetes workflow while waiting for a native Oxide load balancer.

This implementation currently supports externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster,[5] which allows the selected node to forward traffic to a Service endpoint anywhere in the cluster. If that node disappears, the CCM moves the floating IP to another eligible node and updates the internal address in the Service status.

When Oxide introduces a native load-balancing service, we can update the service controller to use it without changing the Kubernetes interface. Customers will continue creating the same LoadBalancer services and only the infrastructure behind them will change.

How do I use Oxide storage in Kubernetes?

With clusters provisioned, reconciled with Oxide, and reachable from outside their VPCs, storage for stateful workloads became the next layer to address. Kubernetes users request persistent storage through PersistentVolumeClaim objects and expect a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver to create, attach, and mount the underlying volumes. Oxide had disks, but Kubernetes had no native way to manage their lifecycle.

Without an Oxide CSI driver, customers could deploy a third-party Kubernetes storage system such as Longhorn. Longhorn provides its own CSI driver and replicates data across disks attached to Kubernetes workers. However, using Longhorn meant backing its replicas with Oxide distributed disks, which already store three replicas on distinct sleds.

Layering one replicated storage system on another can create substantial write fan-out. When a three-replica Longhorn volume is backed by three-way-replicated Oxide distributed disks, one application write can fan out to as many as nine disk writes. The exact physical write amplification depends on the workload and configuration, but customers wanted to avoid that duplicated replication.

The introduction of Oxide local disks provided a way to remove the second layer of replication. Local disks have no built-in replication and remain tied to their sled, making them well suited to systems such as Longhorn that replicate data across Kubernetes nodes. Our Rancher showcase uses this approach today. It avoids stacking two replicated storage systems, though Longhorn still manages the storage lifecycle rather than a native Oxide integration.

For a native integration, my teammate Luiz wrote RFD 595 Oxide CSI Plugin. The workflow seemed straightforward on paper. When a user creates a PersistentVolumeClaim, the CSI controller creates an Oxide distributed disk. After Kubernetes schedules the pod, the controller attaches that disk to the selected Oxide instance, and the CSI node plugin formats and mounts it for the pod. If the pod is rescheduled onto another node, the controller detaches the disk and reattaches it to the new node.

Prototyping that workflow immediately exposed a blocker. Oxide requires an instance to be stopped before attaching or detaching a disk. Kubernetes, however, expects a CSI driver to attach storage to a running worker after scheduling a pod. Stopping the worker would disrupt every other workload on the node and could trigger cascading scheduling and attachment operations.

Before we can release our CSI plugin, we need to add support for disk hot-plug throughout the Oxide stack, from the hypervisor all the way up to the API. What began as a Kubernetes integration has turned into a project spanning multiple layers of the Oxide software stack.

Disk hot-plug and the Oxide CSI plugin remain under active development as of this writing. In the meantime, customers can use software such as Longhorn with Oxide local disks for dynamically provisioned persistent storage without stacking two layers of replication. When the native CSI plugin ships, customers will be able to use familiar Kubernetes storage APIs backed directly by Oxide distributed disks with replication and durability built in.

What’s next?

The result is not a single Kubernetes integration but a growing ecosystem. Rancher, Omni, and Cluster API provide different paths for provisioning, while the Oxide CCM provides a shared runtime integration for node reconciliation and LoadBalancer services. Customers already use some of these integrations in production, and we dogfood several in our own production workloads. Together, they provide a solid foundation to build on.

Our next step is to expand our dogfooding with the newly released Cluster API provider. Using it to provision and operate more of our clusters will test how these integrations work together day to day.

We still have plenty to build and polish. Our near-term work includes completing disk hot-plug and shipping the CSI plugin, adding autoscaling support, and extending the CCM service controller to support external subnets. Longer term, as we ship resource tagging, OIDC support, and native load balancing, we’ll extend our Kubernetes integrations to take advantage of them.

Building these integrations showed how the architectures of Kubernetes and Oxide complement one another. Kubernetes gives infrastructure providers standard extension points, while Oxide exposes infrastructure primitives through APIs. Oxide’s hardware and software co-design lets us address integration blockers at the layer where they belong and carry the necessary changes through the full stack.

This work also lets us exercise our SDKs and APIs from our customers' perspectives and turn customer friction into product improvements. That feedback loop is how we will continue growing this ecosystem. Customer needs shaped each integration in this post, and they will shape the next one, too.

See it in action

blocks.html_en: What began with those two resources grew into a team effort shaped by a feedback loop. Rather than design integrations in the abstract, we followed the problems customers encountered as they moved from provisioning clusters to operating workloads.

sentences.en: Rancher Node Driver
sentences.zh: Rancher节点驱动程序

blocks.html_en: Before we could maintain the customer-submitted integration, we needed to understand the workflow it supported. I had never used Rancher or worked with a node driver, so reviewing the contribution meant learning both.

sentences.en: Before we could maintain the customer-submitted integration, we needed to understand the workflow it supported.
sentences.zh: 在维护客户提交的集成之前，我们需要了解它支持的工作流程。

sentences.en: I had never used Rancher or worked with a node driver, so reviewing the contribution meant learning both.
sentences.zh: 我从未使用过 Rancher 或使用过节点驱动程序，因此回顾贡献意味着学习两者。

blocks.html_en: A Rancher node driver is an executable plugin that teaches Rancher how to create and manage virtual machines on a particular infrastructure platform. The Oxide Rancher node driver translates those operations into Oxide API requests. Once installed in Rancher, it lets customers provision Oxide instances as nodes in Rancher-managed Kubernetes clusters.

sentences.en: A Rancher node driver is an executable plugin that teaches Rancher how to create and manage virtual machines on a particular infrastructure platform.
sentences.zh: Rancher 节点驱动程序是一个可执行插件，教 Rancher 如何在特定基础设施平台上创建和管理虚拟机。

sentences.en: The Oxide Rancher node driver translates those operations into Oxide API requests.
sentences.zh: Oxide Rancher 节点驱动程序将这些操作转换为 Oxide API 请求。

sentences.en: Once installed in Rancher, it lets customers provision Oxide instances as nodes in Rancher-managed Kubernetes clusters.
sentences.zh: 一旦安装在 Rancher 中，客户就可以将 Oxide 实例配置为 Rancher 管理的 Kubernetes 集群中的节点。

sentences.en: Omni Infrastructure Provider
sentences.zh: 全方位基础设施提供商

blocks.html_en: Customers expressed interest in using Sidero Labs' Omni to provision Kubernetes clusters running Talos Linux. Omni connects to infrastructure platforms through infrastructure providers, programs that create Talos Linux instances and register them with Omni.

sentences.en: Customers expressed interest in using Sidero Labs' Omni to provision Kubernetes clusters running Talos Linux.
sentences.zh: 客户表示有兴趣使用 Sidero Labs 的 Omni 来配置运行 Talos Linux 的 Kubernetes 集群。

sentences.en: Omni connects to infrastructure platforms through infrastructure providers, programs that create Talos Linux instances and register them with Omni.
sentences.zh: Omni 通过基础设施提供商、创建 Talos Linux 实例并将其注册到 Omni 的程序连接到基础设施平台。

sentences.en: With KubeCon North America 2025 a few months away, we saw an opportunity to partner with Sidero Labs to build and showcase an Oxide infrastructure provider for Omni.
sentences.zh: 距离 KubeCon North America 2025 还有几个月，我们看到了与 Sidero Labs 合作为 Omni 构建和展示 Oxide 基础设施提供商的机会。

sentences.en: We had seven weeks to complete it before our Oxide+Sidero event.[2] Building against a second provisioning platform would also test Oxide’s APIs across distinct customer workflows.
sentences.zh: 在 Oxide+Sidero 活动之前，我们有七周的时间来完成它。[2]针对第二个配置平台进行构建还将跨不同的客户工作流程测试 Oxide 的 API。

blocks.html_en: The integration work uncovered several issues across Omni and Talos Linux. I brought those issues to Sidero Labs in siderolabs/omni#1633, where their team was eager to work with us—​a lovely reminder of RFD 68 Partnership as Shared Values.

sentences.en: The integration work uncovered several issues across Omni and Talos Linux.
sentences.zh: 集成工作发现了 Omni 和 Talos Linux 中的几个问题。

sentences.en: I brought those issues to Sidero Labs in siderolabs/omni#1633, where their team was eager to work with us—​a lovely reminder of RFD 68 Partnership as Shared Values.
sentences.zh: 我将这些问题提交给了 siderolabs/omni#1633 中的 Sidero Labs，他们的团队渴望与我们合作——这是 RFD 68 合作伙伴关系作为共同价值观的可爱提醒。

blocks.html_en: The most memorable issue was siderolabs/talos#11948. Oxide uses a FAT12 filesystem for cloud-init user-data, not ISO 9660, but Talos’s filesystem probe only attempted to read an ISO 9660 superblock from the NoCloud configuration disk. When that read failed, the probe stopped instead of trying other formats such as VFAT or MS-DOS. As a result, Talos never read the Oxide user-data containing the configuration needed to join Omni. The fix would not be released in time for KubeCon, leaving us with a rather funny workaround.

sentences.en: The most memorable issue was siderolabs/talos#11948.
sentences.zh: 最难忘的一期是 siderolabs/talos#11948。

sentences.en: Oxide uses a FAT12 filesystem for cloud-init user-data, not ISO 9660, but Talos’s filesystem probe only attempted to read an ISO 9660 superblock from the NoCloud configuration disk.
sentences.zh: Oxide 使用 FAT12 文件系统来存储云初始化用户数据，而不是 ISO 9660，但 Talos 的文件系统探测仅尝试从 NoCloud 配置磁盘读取 ISO 9660 超级块。

sentences.en: When that read failed, the probe stopped instead of trying other formats such as VFAT or MS-DOS.
sentences.zh: 当读取失败时，探测停止，而不是尝试其他格式，例如 VFAT 或 MS-DOS。

sentences.en: As a result, Talos never read the Oxide user-data containing the configuration needed to join Omni.
sentences.zh: 因此，Talos 永远不会读取包含加入 Omni 所需配置的 Oxide 用户数据。

sentences.en: The fix would not be released in time for KubeCon, leaving us with a rather funny workaround.
sentences.zh: 该修复程序无法在 KubeCon 上及时发布，给我们留下了一个相当有趣的解决方法。

blocks.html_en: The workaround right now is to pad the user-data with comments to increase its size enough that it uses an ISO 9660 superblock.

sentences.en: The workaround right now is to pad the user-data with comments to increase its size enough that it uses an ISO 9660 superblock.
sentences.zh: 现在的解决方法是用注释填充用户数据，以增加其大小，使其足以使用 ISO 9660 超级块。

blocks.html_en: The workaround right now is to pad the user-data with comments to increase its size enough that it uses an ISO 9660 superblock.

sentences.zh: 现在的解决方法是用注释填充用户数据，以增加其大小，使其足以使用 ISO 9660 超级块。

sentences.en: Cluster API Provider
sentences.zh: 集群API提供商

blocks.html_en: We knew we wanted to build an infrastructure provider for Kubernetes Cluster API (CAPI) when we first wrote RFD 493 Initial Kubernetes Integrations. Cluster API offered something our first two integrations did not—​an upstream, provider-extensible API for managing clusters without requiring a third-party platform like Rancher or Omni.

sentences.en: We knew we wanted to build an infrastructure provider for Kubernetes Cluster API (CAPI) when we first wrote RFD 493 Initial Kubernetes Integrations.
sentences.zh: 当我们第一次编写 RFD 493 初始 Kubernetes 集成时，我们知道我们想要为 Kubernetes Cluster API (CAPI) 构建一个基础设施提供商。

sentences.en: Cluster API offered something our first two integrations did not—​an upstream, provider-extensible API for managing clusters without requiring a third-party platform like Rancher or Omni.
sentences.zh: Cluster API 提供了我们前两个集成所没有的东西——一个上游、提供商可扩展的 API，用于管理集群，而不需要 Rancher 或 Omni 等第三方平台。

blocks.html_en: CAPI lets operators declaratively create, scale, upgrade, and delete Kubernetes clusters through Kubernetes custom resources. Infrastructure providers handle the platform-specific work, such as creating and deleting virtual machines. Building one is a significant investment. At the time, customer demand and engineering capacity did not yet justify that investment, so the project was deferred.

sentences.en: CAPI lets operators declaratively create, scale, upgrade, and delete Kubernetes clusters through Kubernetes custom resources.
sentences.zh: CAPI 允许操作员通过 Kubernetes 自定义资源以声明方式创建、扩展、升级和删除 Kubernetes 集群。

sentences.en: Infrastructure providers handle the platform-specific work, such as creating and deleting virtual machines.
sentences.zh: 基础设施提供商处理特定于平台的工作，例如创建和删除虚拟机。

sentences.en: Building one is a significant investment.
sentences.zh: 建设一个是一项重大投资。

sentences.en: At the time, customer demand and engineering capacity did not yet justify that investment, so the project was deferred.
sentences.zh: 当时，客户需求和工程能力尚无法证明该投资的合理性，因此该项目被推迟。

blocks.html_en: Eventually, both changed. Customers began asking for a CAPI provider, and the Solutions Software Engineering team grew. My teammates Josh and Brandon took ownership of the work and released Cluster API Provider Oxide (CAPOx), giving customers a Kubernetes-native way to provision clusters on Oxide.

sentences.en: Eventually, both changed.
sentences.zh: 最终，两人都变了。

sentences.en: Customers began asking for a CAPI provider, and the Solutions Software Engineering team grew.
sentences.zh: 客户开始寻求 CAPI 提供商，解决方案软件工程团队不断壮大。

sentences.en: My teammates Josh and Brandon took ownership of the work and released Cluster API Provider Oxide (CAPOx), giving customers a Kubernetes-native way to provision clusters on Oxide.
sentences.zh: 我的队友 Josh 和 Brandon 接管了这项工作，并发布了 Cluster API Provider Oxide (CAPOx)，为客户提供了一种在 Oxide 上配置集群的 Kubernetes 原生方式。

blocks.html_en: The Cluster API workflow also exercises several of our other integrations, allowing us to dogfood[3] the end-to-end cluster workflow. The Kubernetes Image Builder uses our Packer plugin to create CAPI-ready Oxide VM images, which CAPOx uses when provisioning instances. Clusters provisioned with CAPOx also use the separately installed Oxide cloud controller manager (CCM) to integrate Kubernetes with Oxide at runtime.

sentences.en: The Cluster API workflow also exercises several of our other integrations, allowing us to dogfood[3] the end-to-end cluster workflow.
sentences.zh: 集群 API 工作流程还运用了我们的其他几个集成，使我们能够对端到端集群工作流程进行测试[3]。

sentences.en: The Kubernetes Image Builder uses our Packer plugin to create CAPI-ready Oxide VM images, which CAPOx uses when provisioning instances.
sentences.zh: Kubernetes Image Builder 使用我们的 Packer 插件来创建 CAPI 就绪的 Oxide VM 映像，CAPOx 在配置实例时使用该映像。

sentences.en: Clusters provisioned with CAPOx also use the separately installed Oxide cloud controller manager (CCM) to integrate Kubernetes with Oxide at runtime.
sentences.zh: 使用 CAPOx 配置的集群还使用单独安装的 Oxide 云控制器管理器 (CCM) 在运行时将 Kubernetes 与 Oxide 集成。

blocks.html_en: If you want to provision Kubernetes clusters on Oxide with Cluster API, see our Cluster API guide to get started.

sentences.en: If you want to provision Kubernetes clusters on Oxide with Cluster API, see our Cluster API guide to get started.
sentences.zh: 如果您想使用 Cluster API 在 Oxide 上配置 Kubernetes 集群，请参阅我们的 Cluster API 指南以开始使用。

sentences.en: How does Kubernetes track Oxide instances?
sentences.zh: Kubernetes 如何跟踪 Oxide 实例？

blocks.html_en: Provisioning integrations create and manage Oxide instances, but they do not reconcile those instances with Kubernetes Node objects. Without that reconciliation, a cluster could not reliably determine whether an unreachable Kubernetes node was temporarily unavailable or whether its backing Oxide instance had been deleted.

sentences.en: Provisioning integrations create and manage Oxide instances, but they do not reconcile those instances with Kubernetes Node objects.
sentences.zh: 供应集成创建和管理 Oxide 实例，但它们不会将这些实例与 Kubernetes Node 对象进行协调。

sentences.en: Without that reconciliation, a cluster could not reliably determine whether an unreachable Kubernetes node was temporarily unavailable or whether its backing Oxide instance had been deleted.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这种协调，集群就无法可靠地确定无法访问的 Kubernetes 节点是否暂时不可用或其支持的 Oxide 实例是否已被删除。

blocks.html_en: We needed a component that ran in each cluster, spoke to the Oxide API, and continuously reconciled Oxide infrastructure with Kubernetes state. Kubernetes provides a standard extension point for this purpose: the cloud controller manager (CCM). A CCM lets infrastructure-specific controllers integrate Kubernetes resources with an infrastructure provider’s API without adding provider-specific code to Kubernetes itself.

sentences.en: We needed a component that ran in each cluster, spoke to the Oxide API, and continuously reconciled Oxide infrastructure with Kubernetes state.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一个在每个集群中运行的组件，与 Oxide API 交互，并持续协调 Oxide 基础设施与 Kubernetes 状态。

sentences.en: Kubernetes provides a standard extension point for this purpose: the cloud controller manager (CCM).
sentences.zh: Kubernetes 为此提供了一个标准扩展点：云控制器管理器 (CCM)。

sentences.en: A CCM lets infrastructure-specific controllers integrate Kubernetes resources with an infrastructure provider’s API without adding provider-specific code to Kubernetes itself.
sentences.zh: CCM 允许特定于基础设施的控制器将 Kubernetes 资源与基础设施提供商的 API 集成，而无需向 Kubernetes 本身添加特定于提供商的代码。

blocks.html_en: We built the Oxide cloud controller manager to connect Kubernetes with Oxide. Its node controller keeps Kubernetes Node objects synchronized with their backing Oxide instances, recording details such as instance IDs and network addresses, and reporting whether each instance is running, shut down, or no longer exists. Kubernetes uses this information to initialize nodes and safely remove them when their backing instances are deleted.

sentences.en: We built the Oxide cloud controller manager to connect Kubernetes with Oxide.
sentences.zh: 我们构建了 Oxide 云控制器管理器来连接 Kubernetes 和 Oxide。

sentences.en: Its node controller keeps Kubernetes Node objects synchronized with their backing Oxide instances, recording details such as instance IDs and network addresses, and reporting whether each instance is running, shut down, or no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 它的节点控制器使 Kubernetes Node 对象与其支持的 Oxide 实例保持同步，记录实例 ID 和网络地址等详细信息，并报告每个实例是否正在运行、关闭或不再存在。

sentences.en: Kubernetes uses this information to initialize nodes and safely remove them when their backing instances are deleted.
sentences.zh: Kubernetes 使用此信息来初始化节点，并在删除其支持实例时安全地删除它们。

blocks.html_en: The CCM does not create instances or provision clusters. That remains the job of provisioning integrations such as the Rancher node driver, the Omni infrastructure provider, and CAPOx. Instead, it provides a runtime integration shared across those provisioning workflows.

sentences.en: The CCM does not create instances or provision clusters.
sentences.zh: CCM 不创建实例或配置集群。

sentences.en: That remains the job of provisioning integrations such as the Rancher node driver, the Omni infrastructure provider, and CAPOx.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是配置集成（例如 Rancher 节点驱动程序、Omni 基础设施提供商和 CAPOx）的工作。

sentences.en: Instead, it provides a runtime integration shared across those provisioning workflows.
sentences.zh: 相反，它提供了在这些配置工作流程之间共享的运行时集成。

blocks.html_en: Importantly, building the CCM gave us a durable extension point inside each cluster. As Oxide evolves, we can add new infrastructure-aware controllers to the CCM rather than update every provisioning integration.

sentences.en: Importantly, building the CCM gave us a durable extension point inside each cluster.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，构建 CCM 为我们在每个集群内提供了一个持久的扩展点。

sentences.en: As Oxide evolves, we can add new infrastructure-aware controllers to the CCM rather than update every provisioning integration.
sentences.zh: 随着 Oxide 的发展，我们可以向 CCM 添加新的基础设施感知控制器，而不是更新每个配置集成。

blocks.html_en: With that runtime extension point in place, we could address another layer of the Kubernetes experience: exposing applications. The CCM architecture also defines a service controller for Kubernetes LoadBalancer services, giving us a place to address the next customer problem.

sentences.en: With that runtime extension point in place, we could address another layer of the Kubernetes experience: exposing applications.
sentences.zh: 有了运行时扩展点，我们就可以解决 Kubernetes 体验的另一层问题：公开应用程序。

sentences.en: The CCM architecture also defines a service controller for Kubernetes LoadBalancer services, giving us a place to address the next customer problem.
sentences.zh: CCM架构还为Kubernetes LoadBalancer服务定义了服务控制器，为我们提供了解决下一个客户问题的地方。

sentences.en: How do I use LoadBalancer services?
sentences.zh: 如何使用负载均衡服务？

blocks.html_en: One of the capabilities customers expect from cloud-integrated Kubernetes is support for Service objects of type LoadBalancer. When a user creates one, Kubernetes asks the cloud provider’s service controller to provision the necessary infrastructure and publish its address in the Service status. There was just one problem: Oxide did not yet offer a native load balancer.

sentences.en: One of the capabilities customers expect from cloud-integrated Kubernetes is support for Service objects of type LoadBalancer.
sentences.zh: 客户期望云集成 Kubernetes 提供的功能之一是支持 LoadBalancer 类型的服务对象。

sentences.en: When a user creates one, Kubernetes asks the cloud provider’s service controller to provision the necessary infrastructure and publish its address in the Service status.
sentences.zh: 当用户创建一个时，Kubernetes 会要求云提供商的服务控制器提供必要的基础设施并在服务状态中发布其地址。

sentences.en: There was just one problem: Oxide did not yet offer a native load balancer.
sentences.zh: 只有一个问题：Oxide 尚未提供原生负载均衡器。

blocks.html_en: Oxide did, however, have floating IPs. Floating IPs are addresses from a rack’s external IP pools that can be attached to and detached from instances, making those instances reachable from outside their VPCs. A floating IP would deliver traffic to a single Kubernetes node, and the Kubernetes Service dataplane could distribute that traffic to the appropriate pods.

sentences.en: How do I use Oxide storage in Kubernetes?
sentences.zh: 如何在 Kubernetes 中使用 Oxide 存储？

blocks.html_en: With clusters provisioned, reconciled with Oxide, and reachable from outside their VPCs, storage for stateful workloads became the next layer to address. Kubernetes users request persistent storage through PersistentVolumeClaim objects and expect a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver to create, attach, and mount the underlying volumes. Oxide had disks, but Kubernetes had no native way to manage their lifecycle.

sentences.en: With clusters provisioned, reconciled with Oxide, and reachable from outside their VPCs, storage for stateful workloads became the next layer to address.
sentences.zh: 通过配置集群、与 Oxide 协调并可从 VPC 外部访问集群，有状态工作负载的存储成为下一个需要解决的层。

sentences.en: Kubernetes users request persistent storage through PersistentVolumeClaim objects and expect a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver to create, attach, and mount the underlying volumes.
sentences.zh: Kubernetes 用户通过 PersistentVolumeClaim 对象请求持久存储，并期望容器存储接口 (CSI) 驱动程序来创建、附加和挂载底层卷。

sentences.en: Oxide had disks, but Kubernetes had no native way to manage their lifecycle.
sentences.zh: Oxide 有磁盘，但 Kubernetes 没有本地方法来管理其生命周期。

blocks.html_en: Without an Oxide CSI driver, customers could deploy a third-party Kubernetes storage system such as Longhorn. Longhorn provides its own CSI driver and replicates data across disks attached to Kubernetes workers. However, using Longhorn meant backing its replicas with Oxide distributed disks, which already store three replicas on distinct sleds.

sentences.en: Without an Oxide CSI driver, customers could deploy a third-party Kubernetes storage system such as Longhorn.
sentences.zh: 如果没有 Oxide CSI 驱动程序，客户可以部署第三方 Kubernetes 存储系统，例如 Longhorn。

sentences.en: Longhorn provides its own CSI driver and replicates data across disks attached to Kubernetes workers.
sentences.zh: Longhorn 提供自己的 CSI 驱动程序，并在连接到 Kubernetes 工作线程的磁盘之间复制数据。

sentences.en: However, using Longhorn meant backing its replicas with Oxide distributed disks, which already store three replicas on distinct sleds.
sentences.zh: 然而，使用 Longhorn 意味着使用 Oxide 分布式磁盘支持其副本，该磁盘已经在不同的雪橇上存储了三个副本。

blocks.html_en: Layering one replicated storage system on another can create substantial write fan-out. When a three-replica Longhorn volume is backed by three-way-replicated Oxide distributed disks, one application write can fan out to as many as nine disk writes. The exact physical write amplification depends on the workload and configuration, but customers wanted to avoid that duplicated replication.

sentences.zh: 将一个复制存储系统分层放置在另一个存储系统上可能会产生大量写入扇出。

sentences.en: When a three-replica Longhorn volume is backed by three-way-replicated Oxide distributed disks, one application write can fan out to as many as nine disk writes.
sentences.zh: 当三副本 Longhorn 卷由三向复制 Oxide 分布式磁盘支持时，一个应用程序写入可以扇出至多达 9 个磁盘写入。

sentences.en: The exact physical write amplification depends on the workload and configuration, but customers wanted to avoid that duplicated replication.
sentences.zh: 确切的物理写入放大取决于工作负载和配置，但客户希望避免重复复制。

blocks.html_en: The introduction of Oxide local disks provided a way to remove the second layer of replication. Local disks have no built-in replication and remain tied to their sled, making them well suited to systems such as Longhorn that replicate data across Kubernetes nodes. Our Rancher showcase uses this approach today. It avoids stacking two replicated storage systems, though Longhorn still manages the storage lifecycle rather than a native Oxide integration.

sentences.zh: Oxide 本地磁盘的引入提供了一种消除第二层复制的方法。

sentences.en: Our Rancher showcase uses this approach today.

sentences.en: It avoids stacking two replicated storage systems, though Longhorn still manages the storage lifecycle rather than a native Oxide integration.

blocks.html_en: For a native integration, my teammate Luiz wrote RFD 595 Oxide CSI Plugin. The workflow seemed straightforward on paper. When a user creates a PersistentVolumeClaim, the CSI controller creates an Oxide distributed disk. After Kubernetes schedules the pod, the controller attaches that disk to the selected Oxide instance, and the CSI node plugin formats and mounts it for the pod. If the pod is rescheduled onto another node, the controller detaches the disk and reattaches it to the new node.

sentences.zh: 如果 Pod 被重新调度到另一个节点，控制器会分离磁盘并将其重新附加到新节点。

content_html_zh:
2024 年底，客户和潜在客户渴望在 Oxide 上运行 Kubernetes，但我们没有支持的集成来帮助他们做到这一点。

Kubernetes 和 Oxide 是天生的一对。 Kubernetes 通过标准扩展点定义了它期望的基础设施行为，而 Oxide 通过 API 公开了实现该行为所需的原语。 整合的基础就在那里。 缺少的是软件以及对客户实际需要哪些集成的了解。

这就是我作为第一位解决方案软件工程师加入 Oxide 时的情况，[1] 专注于构建软件来解决客户问题。 我的第一个任务是让在 Oxide 上部署和操作 Kubernetes 变得更加容易。

在第一周，我获得了两个资源来帮助我入门：

  1. 客户提交的 Rancher 节点驱动程序拉取请求
  2. RFD 493 初始 Kubernetes 集成的早期草案

从这两种资源开始，逐渐发展成为由反馈循环形成的团队努力。 我们没有抽象地设计集成，而是跟踪客户从配置集群转向操作工作负载时遇到的问题。

这篇文章在整个 Kubernetes 生命周期中跟踪这些问题，而不是严格按时间顺序排列。 不同的配置工作流程让我们想到了 Rancher、Omni 和 Cluster API。 运行集群需要基础设施协调，暴露应用程序暴露网络差距，有状态工作负载暴露存储限制。 在每个阶段，客户工作流程都会暴露出下一个差距，从而塑造我们构建的集成和未来的平台工作。

如何在 Oxide 上配置 Kubernetes 集群？

我们解决的第一个差距是配置。 我们的近期目标是解除对提交 Rancher 节点驱动程序拉取请求的客户的封锁。 通过研究他们的用例还可以让我们获得在 Oxide 上创建 Kubernetes 集群的第一手经验，并帮助我们发现下一个需要解决的问题。

没有一种配置方法适合所有客户的工作流程，因此我们最终发布了三个集成。

Rancher节点驱动程序

在维护客户提交的集成之前，我们需要了解它支持的工作流程。 我从未使用过 Rancher 或使用过节点驱动程序，因此回顾贡献意味着学习两者。

Rancher 节点驱动程序是一个可执行插件，教 Rancher 如何在特定基础设施平台上创建和管理虚拟机。 Oxide Rancher 节点驱动程序将这些操作转换为 Oxide API 请求。 一旦安装在 Rancher 中，客户就可以将 Oxide 实例配置为 Rancher 管理的 Kubernetes 集群中的节点。

测试证实客户的实施有效。 我合并了拉取请求，添加了 CI/CD 和文档改进，并发布了初始版本。 Oxide 正式进行了首次 Kubernetes 集成，并且客户已经在生产中成功使用它！

全方位基础设施提供商

客户表示有兴趣使用 Sidero Labs 的 Omni 来配置运行 Talos Linux 的 Kubernetes 集群。 Omni 通过基础设施提供商、创建 Talos Linux 实例并将其注册到 Omni 的程序连接到基础设施平台。

距离 KubeCon North America 2025 还有几个月，我们看到了与 Sidero Labs 合作为 Omni 构建和展示 Oxide 基础设施提供商的机会。 在 Oxide+Sidero 活动之前，我们有七周的时间来完成它。[2]针对第二个配置平台进行构建还将跨不同的客户工作流程测试 Oxide 的 API。

集成工作发现了 Omni 和 Talos Linux 中的几个问题。 我将这些问题提交给了 siderolabs/omni#1633 中的 Sidero Labs，他们的团队渴望与我们合作——这是 RFD 68 合作伙伴关系作为共同价值观的可爱提醒。

最难忘的一期是 siderolabs/talos#11948。 Oxide 使用 FAT12 文件系统来存储云初始化用户数据，而不是 ISO 9660，但 Talos 的文件系统探测仅尝试从 NoCloud 配置磁盘读取 ISO 9660 超级块。 当读取失败时，探测停止，而不是尝试其他格式，例如 VFAT 或 MS-DOS。 因此，Talos 永远不会读取包含加入 Omni 所需配置的 Oxide 用户数据。 该修复程序无法在 KubeCon 上及时发布，给我们留下了一个相当有趣的解决方法。

现在的解决方法是用注释填充用户数据，以增加其大小，使其足以使用 ISO 9660 超级块。

KubeCon 到来了，我们举办了 Oxide+Sidero 活动来展示 Omni 的 Oxide 基础设施提供商。 客户现在可以使用该基础设施提供商来配置运行 Talos Linux 的 Oxide 实例作为 Omni 托管 Kubernetes 集群中的节点。

集群API提供商

当我们第一次编写 RFD 493 初始 Kubernetes 集成时，我们知道我们想要为 Kubernetes Cluster API (CAPI) 构建一个基础设施提供商。 Cluster API 提供了我们前两个集成所没有的东西——一个上游、提供商可扩展的 API，用于管理集群，而不需要 Rancher 或 Omni 等第三方平台。

CAPI 允许操作员通过 Kubernetes 自定义资源以声明方式创建、扩展、升级和删除 Kubernetes 集群。 基础设施提供商处理特定于平台的工作，例如创建和删除虚拟机。 建设一个是一项重大投资。 当时，客户需求和工程能力尚无法证明该投资的合理性，因此该项目被推迟。

最终，两人都变了。 客户开始寻求 CAPI 提供商，解决方案软件工程团队不断壮大。 我的队友 Josh 和 Brandon 接管了这项工作，并发布了 Cluster API Provider Oxide (CAPOx)，为客户提供了一种在 Oxide 上配置集群的 Kubernetes 原生方式。

集群 API 工作流程还运用了我们的其他几个集成，使我们能够对端到端集群工作流程进行测试[3]。 Kubernetes Image Builder 使用我们的 Packer 插件来创建 CAPI 就绪的 Oxide VM 映像，CAPOx 在配置实例时使用该映像。 使用 CAPOx 配置的集群还使用单独安装的 Oxide 云控制器管理器 (CCM) 在运行时将 Kubernetes 与 Oxide 集成。

如果您想使用 Cluster API 在 Oxide 上配置 Kubernetes 集群，请参阅我们的 Cluster API 指南以开始使用。

Kubernetes 如何跟踪 Oxide 实例？

供应集成创建和管理 Oxide 实例，但它们不会将这些实例与 Kubernetes Node 对象进行协调。 如果没有这种协调，集群就无法可靠地确定无法访问的 Kubernetes 节点是否暂时不可用或其支持的 Oxide 实例是否已被删除。

我们需要一个在每个集群中运行的组件，与 Oxide API 交互，并持续协调 Oxide 基础设施与 Kubernetes 状态。 Kubernetes 为此提供了一个标准扩展点：云控制器管理器 (CCM)。 CCM 允许特定于基础设施的控制器将 Kubernetes 资源与基础设施提供商的 API 集成，而无需向 Kubernetes 本身添加特定于提供商的代码。

我们构建了 Oxide 云控制器管理器来连接 Kubernetes 和 Oxide。 它的节点控制器使 Kubernetes Node 对象与其支持的 Oxide 实例保持同步，记录实例 ID 和网络地址等详细信息，并报告每个实例是否正在运行、关闭或不再存在。 Kubernetes 使用此信息来初始化节点，并在删除其支持实例时安全地删除它们。

CCM 不创建实例或配置集群。 这仍然是配置集成（例如 Rancher 节点驱动程序、Omni 基础设施提供商和 CAPOx）的工作。 相反，它提供了在这些配置工作流程之间共享的运行时集成。

重要的是，构建 CCM 为我们在每个集群内提供了一个持久的扩展点。 随着 Oxide 的发展，我们可以向 CCM 添加新的基础设施感知控制器，而不是更新每个配置集成。

有了运行时扩展点，我们就可以解决 Kubernetes 体验的另一层问题：公开应用程序。 CCM架构还为Kubernetes LoadBalancer服务定义了服务控制器，为我们提供了解决下一个客户问题的地方。

如何使用负载均衡服务？

客户期望云集成 Kubernetes 提供的功能之一是支持 LoadBalancer 类型的服务对象。 当用户创建一个时，Kubernetes 会要求云提供商的服务控制器提供必要的基础设施并在服务状态中发布其地址。 只有一个问题：Oxide 尚未提供原生负载均衡器。

然而，Oxide 确实有浮动 IP。 浮动 IP 是来自机架外部 IP 池的地址，可以附加到实例或从实例分离，从而使这些实例可以从其 VPC 外部访问。 使用浮动 IP 提供了一种解锁 LoadBalancer 服务的方法。 浮动 IP 将流量传送到单个 Kubernetes 节点，并且 Kubernetes 服务数据平面可以将该流量分发到适当的 Pod。

要实现这一点，需要考虑 Oxide 浮动 IP 对实例的显示方式。 它们在两个重要方面对客人是透明的。 首先，Oxide 将入站流量的目标地址转换为实例的内部 IP，然后再将流量发送到实例。 其次，实例没有配置浮动IP的网络接口。

└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

│ Translates destination to internal IP: 172.30.0.5:80       │

地址转换造成了一个微妙的集成问题。 Kubernetes 服务数据平面需要将节点的内部 IP 视为服务前端，因为这是数据包到达访客时实际携带的目标地址。 因此，服务控制器在 status.loadBalancer.ingress 中发布两个条目：[4]

  1. 代理模式下附加的浮动IP
  2. VIP模式下节点的内部IP

状态条目如下所示：

status:
  loadBalancer:
    ingress:
      - ip: 45.154.216.233
        ipMode: Proxy
      - ip: 172.30.0.5
        ipMode: VIP

因此，kubectl 输出看起来有点不寻常：

$ kubectl get service nginx
NAME    TYPE           CLUSTER-IP       EXTERNAL-IP                 PORT(S)        AGE
nginx   LoadBalancer   10.106.122.233   45.154.216.233,172.30.0.5   80:30605/TCP   37h

用户可以在 EXTERNAL-IP 列中看到浮动 IP 和节点的内部 IP，即使只有浮动 IP 是外部可访问的。 这是一个不完美的抽象，但它允许我们在等待本机 Oxide 负载均衡器时支持常见的 Kubernetes 工作流程。

此实现当前支持 externalTrafficPolicy：集群 [5]，它允许选定的节点将流量转发到集群中任何位置的服务端点。 如果该节点消失，CCM 将浮动 IP 移动到另一个符合条件的节点，并更新服务状态中的内部地址。

当 Oxide 引入原生负载均衡服务时，我们可以更新服务控制器来使用它，而无需更改 Kubernetes 接口。 客户将继续创建相同的 LoadBalancer 服务，只有其背后的基础设施会发生变化。

如何在 Kubernetes 中使用 Oxide 存储？

通过配置集群、与 Oxide 协调并可从 VPC 外部访问集群，有状态工作负载的存储成为下一个需要解决的层。 Kubernetes 用户通过 PersistentVolumeClaim 对象请求持久存储，并期望容器存储接口 (CSI) 驱动程序来创建、附加和挂载底层卷。 Oxide 有磁盘，但 Kubernetes 没有本地方法来管理其生命周期。

如果没有 Oxide CSI 驱动程序，客户可以部署第三方 Kubernetes 存储系统，例如 Longhorn。 Longhorn 提供自己的 CSI 驱动程序，并在连接到 Kubernetes 工作线程的磁盘之间复制数据。 然而，使用 Longhorn 意味着使用 Oxide 分布式磁盘支持其副本，该磁盘已经在不同的雪橇上存储了三个副本。

将一个复制存储系统分层放置在另一个存储系统上可能会产生大量写入扇出。 当三副本 Longhorn 卷由三向复制 Oxide 分布式磁盘支持时，一个应用程序写入可以扇出至多达 9 个磁盘写入。 确切的物理写入放大取决于工作负载和配置，但客户希望避免重复复制。

Oxide 本地磁盘的引入提供了一种消除第二层复制的方法。 本地磁盘没有内置复制，并且仍然与其底座相关联，这使得它们非常适合 Longhorn 等跨 Kubernetes 节点复制数据的系统。 今天我们的 Rancher 展示就使用了这种方法。 它避免了堆叠两个复制存储系统，尽管 Longhorn 仍然管理存储生命周期而不是本机 Oxide 集成。

对于本机集成，我的队友 Luiz 编写了 RFD 595 Oxide CSI 插件。 工作流程在纸面上看起来很简单。 当用户创建 PersistentVolumeClaim 时，CSI 控制器会创建 Oxide 分布式磁盘。 Kubernetes 调度 pod 后，控制器将该磁盘附加到选定的 Oxide 实例，CSI 节点插件会为 pod 格式化并挂载该磁盘。 如果 Pod 被重新调度到另一个节点，控制器会分离磁盘并将其重新附加到新节点。

对该工作流程进行原型设计后，立即暴露了一个障碍。 Oxide 要求在附加或分离磁盘之前停止实例。 然而，Kubernetes 期望 CSI 驱动程序在调度 Pod 后将存储附加到正在运行的工作线程。 停止工作线程会中断节点上的所有其他工作负载，并可能触发级联调度和附件操作。

在发布 CSI 插件之前，我们需要在整个 Oxide 堆栈（从虚拟机管理程序一直到 API）中添加对磁盘热插拔的支持。 最初的 Kubernetes 集成已经变成了一个跨越多个 Oxide 软件堆栈层的项目。

截至撰写本文时，磁盘热插拔和 Oxide CSI 插件仍在积极开发中。 与此同时，客户可以使用Longhorn等软件和Oxide本地磁盘来动态配置持久存储，而无需堆叠两层复制。 当原生 CSI 插件发布时，客户将能够使用由 Oxide 分布式磁盘直接支持的熟悉的 Kubernetes 存储 API，并内置复制和持久性。

接下来是什么？

结果不是单一的 Kubernetes 集成，而是一个不断发展的生态系统。 Rancher、Omni 和 Cluster API 提供不同的配置路径，而 Oxide CCM 为节点协调和 LoadBalancer 服务提供共享运行时集成。 客户已经在生产中使用了其中一些集成，我们在自己的生产工作负载中测试了其中一些集成。 它们共同提供了坚实的基础。

我们的下一步是通过新发布的 Cluster API 提供程序来扩展我们的测试。 使用它来配置和操作更多的集群将测试这些集成如何日常协同工作。

我们还有很多东西需要构建和完善。 我们的近期工作包括完成磁盘热插拔和交付 CSI 插件、添加自动缩放支持以及扩展 CCM 服务控制器以支持外部子网。 从长远来看，随着我们提供资源标记、OIDC 支持和本机负载平衡，我们将扩展 Kubernetes 集成以利用它们。

构建这些集成展示了 Kubernetes 和 Oxide 的架构如何相互补充。 Kubernetes 为基础设施提供商提供标准扩展点，而 Oxide 通过 API 公开基础设施原语。 Oxide 的硬件和软件协同设计让我们能够在其所属层解决集成障碍，并在整个堆栈中进行必要的更改。

这项工作还让我们从客户的角度运用我们的 SDK 和 API，并将客户的摩擦转化为产品改进。 这个反馈循环是我们继续发展这个生态系统的方式。 客户需求塑造了本文中的每一个集成，也将塑造下一个集成。
